A fragment of a Roman copper-alloy finger-ring. The piece represents the bezel and part of the shoulders of the ring. The bezel takes the form of a raised oval plinth, the upper surface of which bears a crudely incised pattern of curves. The sides of the shoulders angle inwards to the points where they are broken off. An incised transverse groove separates the flat area at the base of the bezel…
